title: Answer to Question: The European-American Struggle in North Africa
text:
Answer to Question

The European-American Struggle in North Africa

Question:

My question is about North Africa, and I apologise for it having many aspects, but they are connected as I see them:

1- Matters have become confused for me on the subject of North Africa, and especially Libya. Leon had set 20/9/2015 as a final deadline for the solution between the negotiating parties in Skhirat in Morocco, but just before that, on 19/9/2015, Haftar undertook a military operation in Benghazi, which made the UN envoy Leon criticise this action as if it were intended to provoke and to obstruct reaching a solution. And that is what happened, so another final deadline was set, reaching to 20/10/2015! It is known that Haftar is supported by America, and the Tobruk government is likewise supported by America, and it is negotiating, while Haftar obstructs the negotiation. So what is the explanation of this contradiction?

2- On 7/9/2015 the Spanish Senate officially gave the green light to establishing an American military base in the south of the country (AFRICOM), which America has long tried to establish in North Africa without finding acceptance... And it was announced that the main mission of this new force, according to the new amendment in the Senate, is "intervening by sea, land and air in the various crises in the African continent..." So does that mean that America has decided on struggle with Europe, and especially Britain and France, the two with colonial roots in North Africa? And what is the extent of its success in that?

3- That was preceded and accompanied by intensive visits by the Americans to North Africa, especially Tunisia. So do these intensive visits to North Africa confirm what I mentioned in the second point about the struggle with Europe? And is it possible to explain this struggle in North Africa, "Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya", even if in broad lines, for the question about it is a natural one, especially in the current circumstances? Thank you, and excuse me once again for the length of the question.

Answer:

Your apology is accepted; may Allah forgive us and you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. I will answer you, by the permission of Allah, taking into account the sequence of events:

First: Regarding America's interest in North Africa and the establishment of the AFRICOM base:

1- America has been interested in North Africa since the fifties, not just today. When its ambassadors met in Istanbul in the month of 11/1950 CE and held their first conference in Istanbul, chaired by George McGhee, the Under Secretary in the US State Department for the affairs of the Middle East and North Africa, since that date America has been struggling with Europe to displace it and take its place in its colonies. This struggle intensifies at one time and eases at another according to the international and regional circumstances. The conference lasted five days, and in it they reviewed the most prominent political, strategic and economic situations of this region, and from then began the struggle of the new American colonialism against the old European colonialism... America succeeded in introducing its influence into many areas of the Middle East and the Nile basin at the expense of the European influence, "Britain and France", but its influence did not settle in North Africa, because America's priority was the Middle East region together with the Nile basin...

2- America realises that the political milieu in North Africa belongs to Europe, and that is why it resorted to other means, apart from the usual political actions with the political milieu, to penetrate the region. The most prominent of them are two matters: the first is the subject of terrorism and its exploitation for military agreements, and penetration by way of the army, training and military aid, and then military bases. The second is economic aid and the affiliated international institutions. America kept moving these two matters continuously, except in periods that fall under the heading of the warrior's rest! Among the attempts to establish bases was the decision taken by George Bush the son to establish an American military command in Africa, "AFRICOM": (On 6/2/2007 CE President Bush and Defence Secretary Robert Gates announced the establishment of the United States Africa Command), AFRICOM's page on Facebook... And although this command was made originally to dominate Africa, plunder its wealth and colonise its people, America, in the habit of colonialists, tried to present it as though it were for the protection of Africa. That is why it invited a number of African presidents to attend the celebration of that command! (The Africa Command officially began its activity on 1 October 2008 through a ceremony at the Defence Department, on the basis that the American military command in Africa, usafricom, is a unit composed of unified combatant forces administered by the US Defence Department. Representatives of the African states in Washington DC attended it), from Wikipedia, the free encyclopaedia.

3- America tried hard to establish this base in North Africa in order to dominate it, so that its influence would take the place of European influence there, but it could not, because Europe's agents lay in wait for it, out of loyalty to European influence, and the AFRICOM project remained marking time. When America despaired of implementing it in North Africa as planned, it turned to the north of North Africa and set down its baggage in Spain, on 7/9/2015 (The Spanish Senate officially gave the green light to establishing an American military base for the Marines in the south of the country within the framework of what is known as AFRICOM command), Al-Shorouk Gate, 7/9/2015 CE. This base is not far from North Africa; rather it is on its borders, and it enables them in their malicious plans in the region. The "AFRICOM" project was marketed on the pretext of the global war on "terrorism", but this project carries within it many aims that all flow into entrenching American hegemony over the world. It is not for protecting Africa from the dangers of "terrorism"; rather it is within the framework of the global American strategy to control the sources of oil and wealth and to monitor all the sea passages in the world on the one hand, and to displace the old colonial influence so that the new colonialism takes its place, that is, it is a struggle over sucking the blood and plundering the wealth, on the other hand.

Despite all that, the fact that America has not been able to build the AFRICOM base somewhere in North Africa means that it has not possessed a firm foothold in this region. It tried to establish it in Algeria and met great rebuff... Likewise it was not able to in Morocco, Libya and Tunisia... It is currently focusing on Libya, exploiting the unrest there, and also on Tunisia, exploiting the fragility of the rule there because of the return of the previous political class against which the people originally rose up and which is hated by the people... Even so, it is not easy for the AFRICOM base to be moved to North Africa, because the barrier of fear has been broken among the people, and their keeping silent over the installation of evil bases in their country is unlikely... This does not mean that the work of the AFRICOM base, while it is in Spain, will be far from influencing the political situation in North Africa; rather it is only less influential. That is, America will repeat the attempt time after time, until if it finds a gap it will enter through it, especially in Tunisia and Libya.

Second: Regarding the intensification of visits and the European-American struggle in Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya:

The intensification of visits is nothing but a continuation of the American and European plans in competing over the wealth of the region and its strategic location. America and Europe, as we said above, did not begin their greed in North Africa today, but before AFRICOM, during it and after it... We review some of these actions and plans that America and Europe toss back and forth on the arena of the Muslim lands in North Africa, "Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya":

• Morocco:

a- America supported the (liberation) movements from France in Morocco in order to take its place, and thus it was able to introduce its influence at independence in Morocco in the era of Muhammad V. But this matter did not last long, for after the death of Muhammad V the influence of Britain became the one strongly present, with the coming of Hassan II in 1961 CE. The road to Morocco became closed to America, until it found the opportunity in the Polisario movement for the independence of the Sahara after Spain's departure from it on 26/2/1976 CE, after (91) years of colonisation. Before that, the United Nations, under America's influence, had formed a fact-finding mission and sent it to Western Sahara, and this mission submitted its report to the General Assembly on 9/6/75, recommending in it the independence of the Sahara from Spain, and that the Polisario organisation is the dominant movement in the territory and has considerable influence there. Thus America brought the Polisario to prominence and supported it as the representative of the Sahrawi people, and the purpose of that was that the Sahara should not return to Morocco after Spain's departure from it, so that it would remain a hotspot of tension demanding independence, which America would exploit for its interests in North Africa.

But Hassan II confronted the American plan with the support of Britain, during the period of his rule from 1961-1999 CE, as he was known for his political shrewdness and cunning from the prime of his youth. He was able to lead Morocco strongly and achieve a stability that neighbouring states have been unable to achieve up to now, and he gained popularity to some extent after the Green March to liberate the Moroccan Sahara from Spanish colonialism in 1975.

https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975

b- Spain withdrew from the Sahara on 26/2/1976 CE, and the next day the Sahrawi National Council announced the establishment of the Sahrawi Arab Republic... America began actual intervention immediately after that, by way of its influence in the issuing of UN resolutions relating to the Sahara. But Hassan, with his cunning, and with the English behind him, whenever America tried to provoke him with a resolution, went around it! Thus Hassan absorbed the American pressures without anything changing in the reality of the Sahara. When Hassan II died, his son Muhammad VI succeeded him on 23/7/1999 CE. Like his father he was loyal to Britain, but he is not a man of politics and cunning like his father, so America became active to take possession of him, and so Britain feared for him falling before the labyrinths of the American plans...

c- Britain feared for Muhammad VI in the face of the American pressures and plans, for the king is less cunning than his father and less experienced in plunging into the depths of political life. That is why Britain advised him, "or ordered him", as is its habit in preserving its small agents, not to continue in the hard-line course towards America as his father had. So he showed understanding of what America says about freedom, democracy and human rights, and dealt with America with excessive softness, so that America became Morocco's fourth trading customer and the first dealer outside the European Union, "1.5 billion dollars volume of trade exchange"... And when America proposed, during the NATO summit held in Istanbul in June 2004 CE, granting Morocco the status of a major non-NATO ally, as the first Arab state from North Africa to enter the NATO club, when America proposed that, Britain made him agree to it with caution and wariness, because it realises that America's proposal is to influence Morocco's political situation... Likewise his position towards the American resolutions became not hard-line as his father's was; rather he agrees and procrastinates in implementation. That is why he agreed to Baker's proposal regarding the compromise solution under the name of the third solution, which is in stages, beginning with autonomy for the Sahara, and then after five years a referendum on self-determination, which is the proposal the Security Council approved in its resolution number "1359" on 29/6/2001. He agreed to it, but in the English way, that is, after back-and-forth for a period of seven years, in 2007, and also by calling it a Moroccan initiative! America's plans towards Morocco stopped only for a few years, because of its preoccupation with other priorities, such as its economic crisis that escalated in 2008 and after, as well as the external political and military crises... That was until the spring of 2013, when America began to move the crisis again strongly, to take the Sahara crisis as a pretext for intervention in North Africa and the other African states adjoining it... It prepared a draft project to expand the mission of the UN mission "MINURSO" in the Moroccan Sahara and make it include monitoring human rights in the Sahara, so that it would be a pretext for it to examine every small and large matter in the Sahara on the pretext of human rights! And although the project was postponed for another year under Security Council resolution number "2099" issued on 25/4/2013... America, together with the Secretary-General and his envoy Ross, became active during the year of extension in preparing the atmosphere anew for discussing the referendum and human rights... The American diplomat Christopher Ross, in his capacity as the personal envoy of the UN Secretary-General to Western Sahara, visited the region in the month of October 2013 and then on 28/1/2014, and in his visits Ross was concerned with the subject of the referendum and human rights...

d- Even so, Morocco's position was similar to Jordan's position, of not confronting openly. Later Morocco began to outbid America in the war on terrorism, by confronting it with what is called "moderate religious discourse", since Morocco constitutes an Islamic religious reference, especially for the Maliki madhhab and the Tijaniyyah spread in the states of the Sahel and the Sahara, Mali, Senegal and Niger. Indeed dozens of preachers, khateebs and men of religion were deployed in Senegal, Ivory Coast, Mali and Benin, in addition to receiving 500 pupils for religious studies in Moroccan institutes and universities! America was forced to praise Morocco's role: "The Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in charge of African affairs, Bisa Williams, said in a statement to the Maghreb Arab Press agency, on the sidelines of an international symposium hosted by Nouakchott on the 19th and 20th of this month: (We highly value the Moroccan experience in Africa as a whole, and particularly in the Sahel region, because Morocco has spared no effort so that other countries may benefit from its experience in the field of combating violent extremism)." Hespress: 21/08/2015 CE.

Thus America has not succeeded in exploiting the issue of the Sahara, nor the subject of the referendum and human rights; it has not succeeded in all that, so far, in displacing English influence in Morocco. We say so far because the struggle between America and Europe is continuing in Africa.

• As for Algeria:

It is a state of standing which resisted America's plans more strongly than its neighbour. Since Boumediene's coup against Ben Bella, who was going in America's line together with Abdul Nasser, since that date British influence has been entrenched in Algeria, with some French protrusions which intensified at times, especially in the era of some weak presidents. Boumediene continued in rule from 19/6/1965 until his death on 27/12/1978. After Boumediene's period in Algeria, weak presidents took over rule, so rule came to be in the hand of the army, and those with influence in it were French in loyalty, culture and training. They moved with their coup in 1992 in order to prevent the Islamic Salvation Front from reaching rule after it had succeeded in the elections... They committed several massacres against the Salvation Front in particular and against many Muslims in general, and they were not able to administer the country; rather the people hated and loathed them... During the years of their influence, from 1992 to 1999, there were four presidents, without effectiveness; rather the army was the controlling force. But the army men loyal to France at that time were not able to deal with the consequences of their coup and calm the situation in the country, after they had committed horrific massacres against the Muslim people of Algeria...

In that atmosphere Britain brought Bouteflika from Switzerland and returned him to Algeria, and created a political atmosphere for him as a saviour, exploiting the failure of the army leaders in administration. And because of the people's hatred for them on account of their massacres, the army men agreed with Abdelaziz Bouteflika in 1999 that he would be the president, on condition that no accountability for their crimes and their destruction of the country would touch them, and that he would work to heal the wounds by calling for concord, peace and reconciliation... That is, they resorted to him to save them!... Bouteflika has been president from 1999 until today, and Bouteflika is still in close relationship with Britain, and he crowned that by visiting Britain in 2006, the first visit of an Algerian president to Britain. Although France's group in the Algerian army, who are influential to some extent, realise Bouteflika's relationship with Britain, and also realise that Bouteflika was not in harmony with French policy, for he rejected the Mediterranean Union project that France brought in Sarkozy's era... even so, those loyal to France in the army have not been able to stop his presidency to this day! And although Britain did not fear France for its influence in Algeria as it feared America, it saw fit to end those French protrusions, for that is stronger for its influence. But it proceeded in this matter gradually, because it is not in struggle with France; rather the struggle is with America. That is why those changes of the officers loyal to France passed without heating up the atmosphere, as if there were a struggle! For example, "Lamari, the chief of staff, resigned for health reasons, "or was dismissed", on 3/8/2004 CE, and 48 hours after the resignation Bouteflika dismissed, on 5/8/2004, Major General Ibrahim al-Sharif, the commander of the First Military Region..." And at the beginning of 2014 General Hassan was dismissed from his duties as commander of the counter-terrorism unit in the intelligence, then Bouteflika carried out other dismissals... But those dismissals took place without a hot clash affecting the structure of the regime. What confirms that is that when General Hassan was arrested on 27/8/2015 CE and brought to trial, Ahmed Ouyahia, the director of the office of the President of the Republic, was asked whether this meant a struggle at the top of the pyramid of authority in Algeria, and he denied that, asserting that what is being rumoured is salon talk" (Al Jazeera, 12/9/2015 CE)... And even when Bouteflika relieved, on 13/9/2015, a senior officer of those with French leanings, namely the director of the general intelligence services, Mohamed Lamine Mediène, known as General Toufik, of his duties, that was done without any heat or effect on the structure of the regime! It can be said that Bouteflika succeeded to some extent in these dismissals with Britain's support for him, even though there is still a place for France in the army, since the culture and training of the army are for the most part from France... But, as we said, Bouteflika's "struggle" with the army was soft, taking place quietly, closer to sporting competition, and not affecting the basic issues of the regime. This differs from the real struggle with America and its plans in Algeria to take political possession of Algeria and replace Britain there. For example:

a- After Spain's departure from the Sahara in 1976 CE after 91 years of colonisation, America found the opportunity in the Polisario movement for the independence of the Sahara, and took it as a pretext for intervention in North Africa, and especially Algeria... But the rulers in Algeria, "Britain", were alert to the matter, so they confined the Polisario to a strip at the border and surrounded it with their eyes, because they realised that America had penetrations in it... And until today, despite America's hegemony over the UN missions and envoys regarding the Sahara, it has not been able to take possession of influence in Algeria by way of them.

b- America tried to create a base in Algeria for the forces it established on the pretext of fighting terrorism, namely the forces called "AFRICOM". But Algeria refused, because it, and Britain behind it, realise that this American base is for interfering in the affairs of Algeria. That is why the Algerian Foreign Ministry stated on 3/3/2007: (Algeria is not concerned with hosting the headquarters of the special American forces for Africa, "AFRICOM").

c- It tried once again to raise the subject of fighting terrorism, exploiting the events of Mali on 22/3/2012 CE, and visits took place between it and Algeria to involve Algeria in cooperation with America in combating terrorism, on the pretext that it might reach Algeria. Even so, Algeria, "and Britain behind it", refused America's plan. The most prominent of these visits was the visit of Hillary Clinton, the US Secretary of State, and her meeting with Abdelaziz Bouteflika on 29/10/2012 CE...

d- After Essebsi visited America on 21/5/2015 CE and concluded some agreements with America, and they granted him membership from outside NATO as they had done with Morocco, Jordan and Bahrain, Algeria escalated a strong campaign against these agreements, and the Tunisian President tried to soften the political atmosphere between them, so he sent his special envoy Khemaies Jhinaoui and charged him with a letter to his Algerian counterpart on 24/6/2015..

Algeria's annoyance was not because of Essebsi's visit to America, because all that took place was within an English political plan that Algeria and Tunisia follow. Rather what was intended by it was two matters: giving Tunisia a pretext enabling it to refuse some American demands that are considered a danger to the influence of Europe, "Britain", on the pretext of not clashing with the neighbourhood; and the other matter, sending a strong message to America that Algeria will accept no substitute for Britain, and that it will not accept American influence, and especially the establishment of bases... This was clear from the fact that the annoyance was not a serious objection to Essebsi's visit, the evidence being that Algeria, after Essebsi's envoy met Bouteflika, sent its Foreign Minister Ramtane Lamamra to Tunisia on 13/7/2015 CE on an official visit, according to the statement of the Algerian Foreign Ministry, and the annoyance ended!

• As for Tunisia:

It was under French colonialism, and after that it fell under British influence under the rule of Habib Bourguiba in Tunisia from 1956-1987. By 1987 Bourguiba had reached 84 years and was unable to carry out what was required of him. At that point Zine El Abidine Ben Ali came to power, who was from Bourguiba's inner circle, and he followed in his footsteps by remaining loyal to Britain. America tried on numerous occasions to introduce its influence in place of British influence, but it could not, because the British political class stood in its face... But when the events of the Arab Spring broke out in 2011 and Ben Ali was toppled, the United States considered that a new opportunity for intervention in North Africa. However, both France and Britain arranged the departure of Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, and since Europe controls the political milieu, it was able to guarantee that the basic system in the country remained unchanged, even with the appearance of the Ennahda party in the country! The political milieu in Tunisia is still strongly within British control, through the European Union agreements that tie Tunisia to Europe. Within some four years Europe was able to bring back the ruling class that had been with the regime of Bourguiba and Ben Ali, not by changing the faces as their followers do; rather they surpassed them in shamelessness, and brought back their chiefs with the same faces, in their corruption and their spreading of corruption! So the chief of the wily old hands among the English agents, Essebsi, became President of Tunisia!! This return was a provocation to the people who had revolted against the tyranny, corruption and agency of the previous regime. The people thought they had got rid of their evil, and then there they were, looking down on them anew. So the people revolt in their faces, and the tyrants meet them with repression and emergency measures, as their followers did before... But the barrier of fear has been broken, and the tyrants are no longer able to gag mouths as they did before. So the regime resorted to the pretext of terrorism to frighten the people, with an explosion here and an explosion there, placed by the regime's henchmen, NATO's operatives and the spies of the embassies struggling on the land of Tunisia, the land of heroism and Jihad in the depths of history. And the regime attributed this to unknown terrorists! America became active in this atmosphere, and it is not far from making it or contributing to it. Its embassies became dens for buying the Tunisian politicians who support Europe, and it also became active in penetrating the army. Britain feared that the regime would fall before America, so it instructed it, in its way of protecting its small, weak agents, to bow before America, but without touching Britain's basic interests! And it trusts Essebsi's loyalty, for he is one of the wily old hands among Britain's agents... And this is what happened:

a- Essebsi visited America and met its President Obama on 21/5/2015. Obama discussed in a meeting with Essebsi the situation in Libya and the region, saying: "The United States will soon provide assistance to enable Tunisia to complete the economic reforms" (Russia Today website, 21/5/2015 CE). And because America considers NATO a strong bond for tying its agents to it so that they do not slip away, as it did with Egypt, making it a major non-NATO ally, America likewise considers the alliance "bait" for attracting new agents from Britain. That is why the US State Department announced on 10/7/2015 the completion of the procedures for granting Tunisia the status of a major non-NATO ally, to become America's sixteenth ally, after Morocco, Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait, of Britain's agents...! Thus do the Kafir colonialists struggle in our lands over attracting the traitorous agents among the rulers... This one tries to fix his agents in place and that one tries to hunt them! Were it not for the treachery that nests and breeds in the hearts of those rulers, they would not have responded, and the Kafir colonialists would not have found a foothold for themselves in our lands. "May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?"...

b- In order for Britain to give Tunisia a line of retreat and a justification for Tunisia not submitting to the American pressures, it agreed with Bouteflika on escalating the annoyance because of Essebsi's visit to America and the agreements that were made, in order to achieve two aims: giving Tunisia a pretext enabling it to refuse some American demands that are considered a danger to the influence of Europe, "Britain"; that is why Algeria escalated the protest, indeed magnified it, so that it was a storm of violent wind... And the other matter, sending a strong message to America that Algeria will accept no substitute for Britain, and that it will not accept American influence, and especially the establishment of bases... This was clear from the fact that the annoyance was not a serious objection to Essebsi's visit, the evidence being that Algeria, after Essebsi's envoys met Bouteflika, sent its Foreign Minister Ramtane Lamamra to Tunisia on 13/7/2015 CE on an official visit, according to the statement of the Algerian Foreign Ministry, and the storm scattered and its temperature began to ease gradually!

c- Then the American contacts with the officials in Tunisia continued:

- "The Tunisian Interior Minister, "Najem Gharsalli", expressed in press statements today, Friday, following his meeting with the US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State, "DAS Arvizu", in Tunis, his gratitude and appreciation for the American support for democracy in Tunisia. The Tunisian minister added that "cooperation between his country and the United States will continue, because the common enemy is one, and it is the fight against terrorism"." Misr Al-Arabiya, 28/8/2015 CE.

- "The US Assistant Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs in charge of the Middle East, "Anne Patterson", stated following her meeting on Tuesday morning at the Kasbah with the head of government Habib Essid that "the existing bilateral cooperation regarding close intelligence exchange and continuous information coordination between the two countries on the file of terrorism, in order to secure an effective confrontation of this scourge" was touched upon." Arabesque, 1/9/2015.

- "The US Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy and Human Rights, Tom Malinowski, visited Tunisia on 2/9/2015, accompanied by Anne Patterson, Assistant Secretary of State for Middle East Affairs, and he stated: "The United States remains committed to helping Tunisia strengthen its security capabilities in the field of intelligence, equipment and training. And Tunisia also needs support in the economic field and in achieving development, especially in the regions of the south and the interior regions"." (Saudi Press Agency, 2/9/2015).

- America "appointed a new ambassador extraordinary last July, Daniel Rubinstein, who has held political posts, among them director of the office of Israel and Palestinian affairs in the US State Department. He is proficient in Arabic and Hebrew, and he will also take over responsibility for the work of the embassy in Libya. This means that America gives Tunisia importance for undertaking political work inside it and as a launching point in the North Africa region..." Wikipedia - the free encyclopaedia.

- "Christine Lagarde began a working visit to Tunisia yesterday, Tuesday, to assess the package of reforms that Tunisia has taken, days before the sixth review of the stand-by arrangement worth about 1.7 billion dollars... During her meeting with a number of representatives of civil society, parties and economic institutions, Lagarde called for strengthening the resilience of the banking sector, establishing tax reforms and limiting the bureaucracy that hinders investment." Al-Ayyam website, issue 9649, Wednesday 9 September 2015, corresponding to 25 Dhul Qi'dah 1436 AH.

d- But this humouring of America, the intensive visits, and its having the status of an ally from outside NATO, did not make Tunisia carry out the basic matters for America, out of the loyalty of its "old-new" rulers to Britain. The United States pressed Tunisia to enable it to establish a military base in the country under the cover of terrorism, but the leaders of Tunisia always refused that by order of Britain. The previous and the current rulers refused "to host" the headquarters of the American Africa Command, "AFRICOM", in Tunisia, and so far America has not succeeded in establishing the base in Tunisia because of the loyalty of both eras to Britain! We say so far, because America is continuing the policy of the carrot and the stick with Tunisia, exploiting the fragility of the regime, its corruption and its provocation of the people through the return of the wily old hands among the English politicians in the regime against which the people revolted... until, if America finds a gap through which it can penetrate to extend its influence in Tunisia in place of the influence of the English, or to share it, it will do so...!

• Libya:

a- For long decades America tried to gain influence in Libya but did not succeed, because Gaddafi was loyal to Britain, keen on the continuation of its influence in Libya. Britain got to know him while he was a student at Sandhurst, then it sponsored him and protected him for several decades, and he continued to preserve its interests for it... Thus, until the uprising occurred in Libya in 2011, the United States had no influence in Libya... The United States, "known for pragmatism and the policy of the art of the possible", saw in the developments witnessed by the North Africa region, or what was known as the Arab Spring, starting from Tunisia, then Egypt, then Libya, it saw in them an opportunity for American intervention and for creating an influence of its own that would compete with the European one. Then it tried to exploit the unrest that occurred during the revolutions of the Arab Spring, and it, together with its agents, worked hard to divert them from their course by all kinds of dirty means. So the United States joined the military intervention in order to gain influence in Libya...

b- America realises that the political milieu in Libya is a British creation, and that is why it exerted every effort to keep the political situation in Libya unstable until it is able to create a political class that contends with the European political class, to displace it if it can, or to share power with it effectively... So it thought of mixing up the cards militarily, and the first step was to charge a military man with moving in something resembling a coup against the existing situation, dominated by the National Congress, where the majority were Europe's men... Thus Haftar moved, and his biography speaks of his loyalty to America... Haftar spent about twenty years in the American state of Virginia, where he was "trained" at the hands of the Central Intelligence Agency, and he did not return to Libya until after the revolution of 17 February 2011, in which he played a role, especially in the city of Benghazi, of varying size... Then Haftar moved on 16/5/2014 and launched an attack on armed groups he described as terrorist in Benghazi, in the name of a military operation he called Libya's Dignity, and he continued his skirmishes according to American policy... Then Haftar continued to obstruct any stable political situation in Libya except after it, that is America, has the ample share. And likewise the other side was striving for it, that is Britain, to have the largest portion... So there came to be two governments and two parliaments in the country! The Libyan parliament in Tobruk and the General Congress in Tripoli, and each of them has a military force! Haftar was able to impose on the Tobruk parliament that they adopt him as general commander of the Libyan army with the rank of lieutenant general, and then he was officially sworn in on 9/3/2015. By that the Tobruk government is dominated by America... As for the General Congress and the Tripoli government, those influential in it go along with Europe, and especially the English, and something of France. And with these there are in the Congress Muslim men who are far from the English but lack sufficient political awareness, which makes it easy for Europe's men to take them in the direction they want!

c- America and Europe were tossing solutions back and forth in Libya according to their interests... As for America, it lacks a political milieu in Libya, as we mentioned, for nearly all of it is from the agents of the English and those who revolve around them or go under their umbrella, from some Islamic movements that are not aware of the political games and their grave consequences... That is why America's reliance is on military actions. So there was Haftar, and then his support from Egypt. Indeed Obama's request to Congress to authorise him to undertake military actions in certain cases, it is not unlikely that the subject of Libya is among the items of this request. Reuters reported on 23/2/2015 that Obama sent a letter to Congress saying in it: "The situation in Libya continues to represent an unusual and extraordinary threat to the security and foreign policy of the United States", and it is understood from Obama's letter that America's position in Libya is critical or in danger, and therefore military intervention serves America's interests and saves its agents... Europe had pre-empted that by standing strongly against military intervention in the crisis.
